source_read: PMC HTML (saved text of PMC4550209, NIH author manuscript), read start to end: abstract, sections 1-4.2, Tables 1-2 (as text), acknowledgments and funding, contributors, conflict statement, footnotes, reference list. Figures 1 and 2 (survival curves) are images absent from the text and were not read; the supplementary .doc (sensitivity analyses) is not in the save. The 'Author information' panel is collapsed in the save, so affiliations could not be checked.

design.note: retrospective-cohort fits: the cohort is defined by 1996 admission records and the monthly use timeline is reconstructed by recall at both interviews (the abstract itself calls the data retrospective self-report). The second interview adds a later wave but not prospective outcome measurement.

key_findings.note: Methods › 2.1 and 2.4 ¶1 match. The paper's own '80% followed at least 48 months' sits beside n=277 with 4-year follow-up (Results › 3.2 ¶3), which is 79.1% of 350; a rounding inconsistency inside the paper, not a card error.
Results › 3.2 ¶2; 36 + 14 + 11 = 61. Wilson 95% CI for 61% of 350 recomputed: 55.8 to 66.0%, matches 'about 56 to 66%'.
47/350 = 13.4%, Wilson 10.3 to 17.4%; 47/206 = 22.8%, Wilson 17.6 to 29.0%: both editors' intervals reproduced. 144/350 = 41% followed under 5 years, as the note says.
Results › 3.2 ¶5; 206 - 159 = 47 and (47 x 60 + 159 x 39)/206 = 43.8, consistent with the mean of 44 months.

Table 2 and Results › 3.3 match. Recomputed exp(coef ± 1.96 SE): 1.05-1.74, 1.15-1.91, 0.58-0.97, 0.90-0.97, 0.22-0.39; the printed intervals agree within rounding of the two-decimal coefficients and SEs.

key_findings.correction: The four predictors dropped at p > .65 are correctly placed (Methods › 2.4 ¶3). The age-at-first-use statement (predictor in the 98-person preliminary analysis, not significant in the complete sample) is in Discussion (section 4) ¶9, the last paragraph before 4.1, not ¶7 (¶7 is about self-help and other drugs). The same paragraph number should be corrected in replication.timeline[0], which cites 'Discussion, 2nd and 7th paragraphs' (¶2 is right for the 57% figure; ¶9 for age at first use).

key_findings.note: Methods › 2.2 and Discussion › 4.1 ¶1. The 88% concerns current or recent use at the first interview, not the retrospective timeline, as the card's validity field says.

reporting_issues.note: Independently found the same: Abstract › Results says 25% relapsed in years 2-5, Results › 3.2 ¶3 gives 7 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 15% of the sample. The card's suggested origin (39% minus 13%) gives 26%, not 25%, so it is a plausible guess rather than an exact match; a rough life-table reconstruction from the yearly figures also gives about 15-17 points, so the 25% is not explained by censoring-adjusted estimation either. The survival curve itself (Figure 1) is an image and could not be read.

Independently found. The decisive point is that both 3-year figures share one numerator (anyone with 36 months of continuous abstinence was followed at least 36 months): 26% of 350 is 89-92 people, i.e. 27-28% of 325, not 32%. The card's second argument (equal to the 2-year figure despite 3% relapsing in year 3) is weaker on its own, because with rounding 104/325 is barely attainable; the 26% figure is what rules it out. The 4- and 5-year pairs are internally consistent (73-74 vs 72; 47 vs 47).
Abstract › Methods says 2-3 years later; Methods › 2.1 ¶2 says 2-4 years later.

Accurate: Methods › 2.3 ¶2 says predictors are mostly from the first interview, and ¶5 defines the self-help/other-treatment variable as participation after discharge and before relapse, coded 1/0; no time-varying covariate is mentioned and the main text never discusses timing or immortal time (the unread supplement might). Strictly this is a design and analysis problem rather than an internal inconsistency; it is already carried in risk_of_bias and interpretation_gap.
Methods › 2.4 ¶3: full-model results not presented; sensitivity analyses only described in the supplement as robust.
Methods › 2.1 ¶1 and the abstract mention random sampling within strata; neither proportional allocation nor weights are stated anywhere.

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-E is acceptable, and the domain set and judgments (confounding high; exposure measurement very high; selection, post-exposure interventions, missing data and outcome some concerns; reported result high; overall very high, not less severe than the worst domain) follow from the text. Two remarks for the senior author: (1) this is in substance a prognostic-factor study, and if a claim ever cites the continuing-care or treatment-duration association as an intervention effect, ROBINS-I would be the apt instrument for that result; (2) selection could defensibly be rated high for the descriptive relapse figures, since deaths and people not located (43% of sampled admissions) are plausibly linked to continued use, but some concerns is within reason for the predictor associations.

interpretation_gap.note: 'Substantial' is right. Points (1)-(4) are all supported by the text (Abstract vs Results › 3.2; Methods › 2.3; abstract omits point and re-abstinence results).

missed: Causal wording on treatment duration not flagged: Discussion ¶6 calls the HR 0.93 per month 'a positive effect of longer index treatment duration'. Time in treatment is plausibly a marker of in-treatment response (people still using tend to leave early; 36% used in the first month after discharge or at discharge), so this association is confounded by response, and the card's confounding note and interpretation gap do not name this for the treatment-duration result.

Discussion ¶5 suggests that 3-5-year remission after methamphetamine treatment may not be substantially worse than for other drugs, although the study has no comparison group of people treated for other drugs; this comparative statement rests only on informal comparison with other studies and is not noted in the interpretation gap.
other_notes: Minor text-table discrepancy in the paper: Results › 3.1 ¶1 gives employment as averaging 29% of months, Table 1 gives 29.9; the card uses the table value, which is right.

outcomes.n_outcomes_tested = 17 counts candidate predictors, not outcomes (one primary outcome, plus descriptive point abstinence at five months); the number is a fair multiplicity proxy but the field label does not fit.

The two missing predictor values were replaced by each subject's average across 10 imputed data sets (Methods › 2.4 ¶2), i.e. a single substituted value rather than multiple imputation with pooling; immaterial at two values.

Not on the card and minor: proportional hazards supported (p = .995, Methods › 2.4 ¶3); self-help differences significant within each risk subgroup (p < .01) and interactions with the two risk factors not significant (Results › 3.3, paragraph after Table 2).
